reply: Around the 27.8-second mark at the bottom of your squat, your heels lifted off the floor, shifting the load onto your forefoot and increasing shear stress on your knees. This breakdown reduces your glute and hamstring recruitment, which often stems from limited ankle dorsiflexion. Focus on driving your whole foot flat into the floor and work on ankle mobilizations before your next squat session.
